task: Decide how the orchestrator should route requests: keep weighted keyword routing with confidence flags, or move to model-based classification
context:
Facts about the current router (core/council/referee.py, measured 2026-10-08):
- Routing uses keyword lists per persona in core/council/councils.json. Each keyword is weighted by 1 / (number of personas that list it), multi-word phrases get 1.5x. Tier rules: questions go to tier 0; broad verbs (redesign, decide, migrate, should we...) go to a council; new-capability scope words plus strong matches in two councils go to tier 3; otherwise the best-scoring persona handles it.
- Tuning set (validation/fixtures/routing/cases.json, 50 requests): 50/50 correct after tuning; 28/50 (56%) before the change.
- Held-out set (holdout.json, 20 requests written after tuning, never tuned against): 16/20 (80%). Misses: "Speed up the slow product search query" went to the database architect instead of performance; "Store the session token in an httpOnly cookie" went to the design systems architect (because of the word "token"); "Decide whether to move from SQLite to Postgres" matched no keywords; a tier 3 feature request was treated as tier 1.
- Every plan now reports confidence (low when the top match rests on one keyword, nothing matched, or the runner-up is close) and its evidence. Both held-out specialist misses were flagged low. Agents can override with --council or --persona.
- Planning runs in the CLI (node), the MCP server (python) and the website build; it must stay deterministic, local and dependency-free (Python standard library only), and needs no API key.
- The alternative under discussion: let the calling agent (the model already running Claude Code or Copilot) classify the request, with keyword routing as a fallback, or add an embedding/LLM classifier inside the framework.

independent.stance: Keep deterministic weighted-keyword routing as the framework's core router. Do not add an embedded LLM or embedding classifier. Add one optional, additive path: the calling agent may pass --council/--persona (already supported) as an override after reading the plan's confidence and evidence. Pilot that agent-assist path for a bounded period and measure it before changing the core.
keyArguments: Smallest change: the override flags and low-confidence 'Check:' prompt already exist (VERIFIED_FACT: core/orchestrator/dispatch.py lines 81 and 143-145 handle confidence and --council/--persona). The calling model is already in the loop, so no new classifier is needed inside the framework.

Boundary: an in-framework LLM or embedding classifier would break the constraint of deterministic, local, stdlib-only and no API key, across three runtimes (CLI node, MCP python, website build). That constraint is stated in the shared context, so I am treating it as a given requirement. I did not check it against the code.

Evidence is limited, so the case for a rewrite is weak. The held-out set is 16/20 (80%), n=20, from the shared context. Both specialist misses were flagged low confidence, so the fallback to agent judgment already triggers where it is needed. The tier-3-as-tier-1 miss is the one gap the confidence flag may not cover. I did not verify that.
The 28/50 to 50/50 gain on the tuning set is partly overfit by construction. The 80% held-out figure is the honest estimate, and its confidence interval is wide (ESTIMATE).
Regret in a year: a model dependency in the router makes results non-reproducible, hard to test (validation/universal-tests/test_routing_eval.py gates on fixed cases) and API-key gated.
risks: Agents may ignore low-confidence flags, so misroutes persist silently.
Keyword lists grow and drift as personas are added, and overlap weights shift.
The held-out set of 20 is too small to distinguish 80% from 90%.
The tier 3 under-escalation miss may not be flagged low.

challenges.critique: The group treats 'misroutes are visible' as settled, but the calibration gate covers only one failure class. VERIFIED_FACT: in validation/universal-tests/test_routing_eval.py (line 57-59) the low-confidence assertion applies only when case tier == 1 and the plan is tier 1 and wrong. A tier mismatch, such as the held-out tier 3 request planned as tier 1, is never checked for a low flag. The CLI 'Check:' line (dispatch.py lines 143-145) only shows when confidence is low and tier > 0. Failures are mostly visible. Both held-out specialist misses were flagged low (task context), and a probe of the tier-3-style request returned tier 1 with confidence low (run by several personas in round 3).

Only the deterministic router can be gated in CI: validation/universal-tests/test_routing_eval.py asserts tuning >=0.95, holdout >=0.75 and low flags on wrong specialists (test-quality-engineer, round 1).

evidence.statement: dispatch.py reports confidence and prints a Check hint pointing to --council and --persona only when confidence is low and tier > 0.
The eval asserts the low flag only for wrong specialists on the holdout, so wrong tiers are not gated.
The request 'Add a new feature for team comments with mentions, permissions and email digests' was routed to tier 1 (security-engineer, keyword 'permission') with confidence low.
evidence.source: node bin/cli.js ask --json, run in round 3

evidence.statement: With n=20 the holdout accuracy interval is roughly 58 to 92 percent.
Whether agents follow the low-confidence flag, and whether adapters other than the Claude plugin tell them the override exists.

assumptions: The calling agent classifies ambiguous requests better than the keyword scorer.
The determinism, keyless and stdlib-only constraint is non-negotiable for all three runtimes.
The held-out cases are representative of real requests.
Misroutes are cheap to recover from because the override flags exist.
unknowns: How often agents honor the low flag and use overrides.
Whether the holdout's own tier-3 case is flagged low (only a similar probe was run).
Whether other adapters (Copilot, others) state the override rule.
The true routing accuracy on real requests beyond 20 held-out cases.

tradeOffs.chosen: Deterministic, local keyword routing with confidence flags
tradeOffs.sacrificed: The extra accuracy a model classifier might give on ambiguous requests
tradeOffs.rationale: Reproducible, testable in CI, keyless and dependency-free in three runtimes.

tradeOffs.chosen: A one-off recorded comparison of agent-assisted routing against keyword-only
tradeOffs.sacrificed: A standing agent-override harness in CI
tradeOffs.rationale: Agent output is not reproducible, so a maintained harness would rot (maintainability-reviewer and test-quality-engineer, round 3).

tradeOffs.chosen: Stop broad keyword tuning; add misses to cases.json only
tradeOffs.sacrificed: Quick gains on the four known held-out misses
tradeOffs.rationale: Avoids overfitting and keeps holdout.json untuned.

risks.description: A wrong tier (such as a tier 3 request planned as tier 1) is not guaranteed to be flagged low, so under-scoped work goes unnoticed.
Agents ignore the low-confidence flag and act on a wrong route.
Keyword lists drift and collide as personas are added.
The holdout becomes a second tuning set, hiding real accuracy.
Tier-0 misroutes get no Check hint because it prints only when tier > 0.

mitigations: Extend test_routing_eval.py so every wrong tier or wrong specialist on tuning and holdout must carry confidence=low, and fix the router if any case fails.
Run the holdout's own tier-3 case and record whether it is flagged low.
Add misses to cases.json only, never holdout.json, with a short contributor recipe (reproduce with ask, add case, run eval, read evidence); check first whether one exists.
Check that other adapters carry the one-sentence low-confidence rule before the pilot, and decide on the tier-0 hint using holdout evidence.
Make routing eval failure messages name the case, the expected and actual persona, and the keywords that fired.
mvpScope: Extend the routing eval with the tier-error low-confidence assertion (a few lines).
Add the four known held-out misses as named regression cases in cases.json.

Run a one-off recorded pilot: expand the holdout toward 50 cases, have an agent classify with the plan evidence visible (or a scripted agent that honors only the low flag), and compare per tier with keyword-only accuracy.
Verify and, if missing, add one shared sentence of low-confidence guidance to the adapters.
excludedScope: No LLM or embedding classifier inside the framework.
No pluggable classifier interface or second routing path.
No standing agent-override harness or maintained agent dataset in CI.
No broad keyword tuning to chase the four held-out misses.
No new machine-readable 'recheck' field unless the pilot shows the confidence field is insufficient.

validationExperiments.hypothesis: Wrong tier routes on tuning and holdout are already flagged low confidence.
validationExperiments.experiment: Extend the routing eval to assert confidence=low on every wrong tier or specialist and run it.
validationExperiments.passMetric: All wrong tier and specialist cases carry confidence=low; otherwise the router is fixed until they do.

validationExperiments.hypothesis: An agent that sees the plan evidence and acts on low flags routes better than keyword-only.
validationExperiments.experiment: One-off recorded run on a holdout expanded toward 50 cases, comparing agent-assisted and keyword-only accuracy per tier.
validationExperiments.passMetric: A clear gain; the 5-point figure is an ESTIMATE to be set after seeing the noise level. Otherwise end the pilot and leave the router as is.

owners: Router maintainer (referee.py and dispatch.py) for the eval extension and any router fix
Test owner for validation/universal-tests/test_routing_eval.py and the fixtures
Adapter and plugin maintainer for the one-sentence guidance in plugin-skills/ask/SKILL.md and adapters

successMetrics.metric: Wrong tier and specialist routes carrying confidence=low
Held-out accuracy on an expanded set of 50 or more cases
successMetrics.target: at least 85%, or the revisit trigger fires

successMetrics.metric: Agent-assisted gain over keyword-only in the one-off run
successMetrics.target: clear gain, with the threshold set after the noise level is known

conditionsToChange: Revisit if a held-out set of 50 or more cases scores below 85%.
Revisit if the pilot shows agents override more than about 25% of routes without improving accuracy (ESTIMATE threshold).
Reconsider a model classifier only if the keyless, deterministic constraint is lifted for the runtimes.
Reconsider if any wrong tier route cannot be made low confidence with a small router change.

dissent.objection: Final recommendation is Test further rather than Pilot: do not pilot agent assist until a narrow gate exists.
dissent.rationale: The low-confidence assertion covers wrong specialists only, so a wrong tier is not proven to be flagged. The probe returned low, but it is a probe, not a gate (round 3).
dissent.suggestedAlternative: First extend the eval so every wrong tier or specialist carries confidence=low, grow the holdout opportunistically from real misroutes, and add the four known misses as regression cases; at most do a one-off recorded agent run.
